findings.impact: The next implementer must either invent an unsupported authenticity check, expand Task 1 beyond its pure metadata boundary, or silently weaken an explicit required test. The current pure_metadata_implementation_ready claim therefore needs this contract correction.
findings.problem: Task 1 requires tag/index/config/archive substitutions to not parse, but accepts only an identity dictionary whose hash fields are opaque lowercase SHA256 strings. A registry manifest/index digest, Docker config digest and rootfs diffID all have the same sha256:<64hex> representation. A substituted well-formed value plus a recomputed core_sha256 satisfies the specified parser schema. No artifact, descriptor contents, API or Docker evidence is available to establish the claimed object class.
findings.recommendation: Limit Task 1 to exact fields, literal distribution/platform, digest syntax, self-hash consistency and field-value comparison against an expected identity. Wrong encodings or unknown typed fields reject; changed well-formed values mismatch during comparison. Explicitly defer semantic config/manifest/index/archive object authentication to Task 3 with actual authenticated artifact/config/rootfs evidence. Update the continuation summary and clarify the spec test allocation; retain all future actual-artifact authentication requirements.
findings.title: Task 1 promises object-class rejection that a hash-only parser cannot establish
findings.validation: After correction, a same-shaped substituted digest may pass shape validation but must mismatch a different expected identity. Task 3 fixtures must reject a manifest/index digest asserted as the config of the authenticated archive.
